sanskrit: tataḥ samabhavad yuddhaṃ ghorarūpaṃ bhayānakam vismāpanaṃ mahārāja nararākṣasayor mṛdhe
english: Then there arose, O great king, a battle of dreadful form and terrifying aspect—astounding to behold—in the clash between the man and the rākṣasa.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca yatra vaikartanaḥ karṇo rākṣasaś ca ghaṭotkacaḥ niśīthe samasajjetāṃ tad yuddham abhavat katham
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: When Karṇa, the son of Vikartana, and the rākṣasa Ghaṭotkaca closed with each other at the dead of night—how did that battle unfold?

sanskrit: kīdṛśaṃ cābhavad yuddhaṃ tasya ghorasya rakṣasaḥ rathaś ca kīdṛśas tasya māyāḥ sarvāyudhāni ca
english: What manner of fight did that terrible rākṣasa wage? What was his chariot like, and his illusions, and all his weapons?

sanskrit: kiṃpramāṇā hayās tasya rathaketur dhanus tathā kīdṛśaṃ varma caivāsya kaṇṭhatrāṇaṃ ca kīdṛśam pṛṣṭas tvam etad ācakṣva kuśalo hy asi saṃjaya
english: What size were his horses, his chariot-banner, and his bow? What was his armor like, and his throat-guard? Being asked, tell me all this, Saṃjaya, for you are skilled in such telling.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca lohitākṣo mahākāyas tāmrāsyo nimnitodaraḥ ūrdhvaromā hariśmaśruḥ śaṅkukarṇo mahāhanuḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Red-eyed he was, huge of body, copper-faced, with a sunken belly, his hair bristling upward, his beard tawny, his ears like spikes, his jaws enormous.

sanskrit: ākarṇād dāritāsyaś ca tīkṣṇadaṃṣṭraḥ karālavān sudīrghatāmrajihvoṣṭho lambabhrūḥ sthūlanāsikaḥ
english: His mouth was split open to the ears, his fangs sharp, his look terrible, his tongue and lips long and coppery, his brows drooping, his nose thick.

sanskrit: nīlāṅgo lohitagrīvo girivarṣmā bhayaṃkaraḥ mahākāyo mahābāhur mahāśīrṣo mahābalaḥ
english: Dark of limb, red of neck, mountainous in stature, fearsome—of vast body, mighty arms, a huge head, and great strength.

sanskrit: vikacaḥ paruṣasparśo vikaṭodbaddhapiṇḍikaḥ sthūlasphig gūḍhanābhiś ca śithilopacayo mahān
english: His hair was dishevelled, his touch rough, his calves swollen and knotted, his haunches thick, his navel sunk, his bulk loose-fleshed and immense.

sanskrit: tathaiva hastābharaṇī mahāmāyo 'ṅgadī tathā urasā dhārayan niṣkam agnimālāṃ yathācalaḥ
english: He bore ornaments upon his hands, that master of great illusion, and armlets too, wearing upon his breast a golden gorget like a mountain girdled with a garland of fire.

sanskrit: tasya hemamayaṃ citraṃ bahurūpāṅgaśobhitam toraṇapratimaṃ śubhraṃ kirīṭaṃ mūrdhny aśobhata
english: Upon his head shone a diadem, wrought of gold and gleaming, adorned with figures of many forms, bright as an arched gateway.

sanskrit: kuṇḍale bālasūryābhe mālāṃ hemamayīṃ śubhām dhārayan vipulaṃ kāṃsyaṃ kavacaṃ ca mahāprabham
english: He wore earrings bright as the rising sun, a fair golden garland, and a broad cuirass of bronze of great splendor.

sanskrit: kiṅkiṇīśatanirghoṣaṃ raktadhvajapatākinam ṛkṣacarmāvanaddhāṅgaṃ nalvamātraṃ mahāratham
english: His great chariot rang with the sound of a hundred bells, flew red banners and pennons, was sheathed in bearskin, and measured a full nalva across.

sanskrit: sarvāyudhavaropetam āsthito dhvajamālinam aṣṭacakrasamāyuktaṃ meghagambhīranisvanam
english: He stood mounted upon it, garlanded with banners, furnished with every choice weapon, fitted with eight wheels, deep-voiced as a thundercloud.

sanskrit: tatra mātaṅgasaṃkāśā lohitākṣā vibhīṣaṇāḥ kāmavarṇajavā yuktā balavanto 'vahan hayāḥ
english: There the horses that drew it were like elephants, red-eyed and terrible, of color and speed at will, mighty and yoked to the car.

sanskrit: rākṣaso 'sya virūpākṣaḥ sūto dīptāsyakuṇḍalaḥ raśmibhiḥ sūryaraśmyābhaiḥ saṃjagrāha hayān raṇe sa tena sahitas tasthāv aruṇena yathā raviḥ
english: His charioteer was a rākṣasa, Virūpākṣa, with blazing face and earrings, who gathered up the horses in battle with reins bright as the sun's rays; and joined with him he stood, as the sun stands with Aruṇa.

sanskrit: saṃsakta iva cābhreṇa yathādrir mahatā mahān divaspṛk sumahān ketuḥ syandane 'sya samucchritaḥ raktottamāṅgaḥ kravyādo gṛdhraḥ paramabhīṣaṇaḥ
english: Like a great mountain wreathed in a vast cloud, a towering banner reaching to the sky was raised upon his car—a flesh-eating vulture, crimson-headed, most fearful to behold.

sanskrit: vāsavāśaninirghoṣaṃ dṛḍhajyam abhivikṣipan vyaktaṃ kiṣkuparīṇāhaṃ dvādaśāratni kārmukam
english: Drawing back a stout-stringed bow that roared like Indra's thunderbolt—a clear span of a cubit thick and twelve cubits in length—

sanskrit: rathākṣamātrair iṣubhiḥ sarvāḥ pracchādayan diśaḥ tasyāṃ vīrāpahāriṇyāṃ niśāyāṃ karṇam abhyayāt
english: and covering all the quarters with arrows the size of chariot-axles, he bore down upon Karṇa in that night that carries off heroes.

sanskrit: tasya vikṣipataś cāpaṃ rathe viṣṭabhya tiṣṭhataḥ aśrūyata dhanurghoṣo visphūrjitam ivāśaneḥ
english: As he drew his bow, planted firm and standing upon his car, the twang of his bowstring was heard like the crashing of the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: tena vitrāsyamānāni tava sainyāni bhārata samakampanta sarvāṇi sindhor iva mahormayaḥ
english: Terrified by him, O Bhārata, all your armies trembled like the great waves of the sea.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ saṃprekṣya virūpākṣaṃ vibhīṣaṇam utsmayann iva rādheyas tvaramāṇo 'bhyavārayat
english: Beholding that misshapen, terrible one rushing upon him, the son of Rādhā, as though smiling, swiftly came forth to meet him.

sanskrit: tataḥ karṇo 'bhyayād enam asyann asyantam antikāt mātaṅga iva mātaṅgaṃ yūtharṣabha ivarṣabham
english: Then Karṇa advanced against him, loosing shafts against him as he loosed his own from close at hand—like elephant against elephant, like bull-leader of the herd against bull.

sanskrit: sa saṃnipātas tumulas tayor āsīd viśāṃ pate karṇarākṣasayo rājann indraśambarayor iva
english: Tumultuous, O lord of peoples, was that encounter of the two, of Karṇa and the rākṣasa, O king, like the clash of Indra and Śambara.

sanskrit: tau pragṛhya mahāvege dhanuṣī bhīmanisvane prācchādayetām anyonyaṃ takṣamāṇau maheṣubhiḥ
english: Seizing their bows of dreadful sound and mighty force, the two covered each other over, hewing at one another with great arrows.

sanskrit: tataḥ pūrṇāyatotsṛṣṭaiḥ śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ nyavārayetām anyonyaṃ kāṃsye nirbhidya varmaṇī
english: Then with smooth-jointed shafts loosed from bows drawn to the full, each held off the other, piercing through the bronze armor on both.

sanskrit: tau nakhair iva śārdūlau dantair iva mahādvipau rathaśaktibhir anyonyaṃ viśikhaiś ca tatakṣatuḥ
english: Like tigers with their claws, like great elephants with their tusks, the two tore at each other with chariot-lances and with arrows.

sanskrit: saṃchindantau hi gātrāṇi saṃdadhānau ca sāyakān dhakṣyamāṇau śaravrātair nodīkṣitum aśaknutām
english: Cleaving each other's limbs and fitting their shafts to the string, scorched by the volleys of arrows, neither could so much as look upon the other.

sanskrit: tau tu vikṣatasarvāṅgau rudhiraughapariplutau vyabhrājetāṃ yathā vāriprasrutau gairikācalau
english: Their every limb wounded, bathed in floods of blood, the two shone like ochre mountains streaming with water.

sanskrit: tau śarāgravibhinnāṅgau nirbhindantau parasparam nākampayetām anyonyaṃ yatamānau mahādyutī
english: Their bodies pierced by arrow-points, rending one another, those two of great splendor, though they strove, could not make each other waver.

sanskrit: tat pravṛttaṃ niśāyuddhaṃ ciraṃ samam ivābhavat prāṇayor dīvyato rājan karṇarākṣasayor mṛdhe
english: That night-battle that was joined went on long and seemed evenly matched, O king, as Karṇa and the rākṣasa gambled with their very lives in the fray.

sanskrit: tasya saṃdadhatas tīkṣṇāñ śarāṃś cāsaktam asyataḥ dhanurghoṣeṇa vitrastāḥ sve pare ca tadābhavan ghaṭotkacaṃ yadā karṇo viśeṣayati no nṛpa
english: As Karṇa fitted his sharp arrows and shot them ceaselessly, both your own men and the foe were struck with dread by the roar of his bow; yet, O king, Karṇa could not gain the upper hand over Ghaṭotkaca.

sanskrit: tataḥ prāduṣkarod divyam astram astravidāṃ varaḥ karṇena vihitaṃ dṛṣṭvā divyam astraṃ ghaṭotkacaḥ prāduścakre mahāmāyāṃ rākṣasaḥ pāṇḍunandanaḥ
english: Then that best of weapon-knowers brought forth a celestial weapon; and seeing the celestial weapon loosed by Karṇa, the rākṣasa Ghaṭotkaca, son of a Pāṇḍava, brought forth a mighty illusion.

sanskrit: śūlamudgaradhāriṇyā śailapādapahastayā rakṣasāṃ ghorarūpāṇāṃ mahatyā senayā vṛtaḥ
english: He appeared encircled by a vast host of rākṣasas of dreadful form, bearing spears and mallets, and crags and trees in their hands.

sanskrit: tam udyatamahācāpaṃ dṛṣṭvā te vyathitā nṛpāḥ bhūtāntakam ivāyāntaṃ kāladaṇḍogradhāriṇam
english: Beholding him with his great bow upraised, those kings were shaken, as though Death the ender of beings were coming on, wielding the terrible rod of Time.

sanskrit: ghaṭotkacapramuktena siṃhanādena bhīṣitāḥ prasusruvur gajā mūtraṃ vivyathuś ca narā bhṛśam
english: Affrighted by the lion-roar that Ghaṭotkaca sent forth, the elephants let flow their urine, and the men were sorely shaken.

sanskrit: tato 'śmavṛṣṭir atyugrā mahaty āsīt samantataḥ ardharātre 'dhikabalair vimuktā rakṣasāṃ balaiḥ
english: Then a most fierce and mighty rain of stones fell on every side, loosed at midnight by the overwhelming forces of the rākṣasas.

sanskrit: āyasāni ca cakrāṇi bhuśuṇḍyaḥ śaktitomarāḥ patanty aviralāḥ śūlāḥ śataghnyaḥ paṭṭiśās tathā
english: Iron discs, fire-tubes, lances and javelins, spears, śataghnīs and pikes fell thick and unbroken.

sanskrit: tad ugram atiraudraṃ ca dṛṣṭvā yuddhaṃ narādhipāḥ putrāś ca tava yodhāś ca vyathitā vipradudruvuḥ
english: Beholding that grim and most savage fight, the kings, and your sons, and the warriors, shaken with terror, fled in all directions.

sanskrit: tatraiko 'strabalaślāghī karṇo mānī na vivyathe vyadhamac ca śarair māyāṃ ghaṭotkacavinirmitām
english: There Karṇa alone, proud and exulting in the might of his weapons, did not waver, but scattered with his shafts the illusion that Ghaṭotkaca had wrought.

sanskrit: māyāyāṃ tu prahīṇāyām amarṣāt sa ghaṭotkacaḥ visasarja śarān ghorān sūtaputraṃ ta āviśan
english: And when his illusion was undone, Ghaṭotkaca in his fury loosed dreadful arrows, and they entered the son of the sūta.

sanskrit: tatas te rudhirābhyaktā bhittvā karṇaṃ mahāhave viviśur dharaṇīṃ bāṇāḥ saṃkruddhā iva pannagāḥ
english: Then those arrows, drenched in blood, having pierced Karṇa in that great battle, entered the earth like serpents enraged.

sanskrit: sūtaputras tu saṃkruddho laghuhastaḥ pratāpavān ghaṭotkacam atikramya bibheda daśabhiḥ śaraiḥ
english: But the son of the sūta, in great wrath, swift of hand and full of valor, overpassing Ghaṭotkaca's onset, pierced him with ten arrows.

sanskrit: ghaṭotkaco vinirbhinnaḥ sūtaputreṇa marmasu cakraṃ divyaṃ sahasrāram agṛhṇād vyathito bhṛśam
english: Ghaṭotkaca, struck through in his vital parts by the sūta's son and sorely pained, took up a celestial discus of a thousand spokes.

sanskrit: kṣurāntaṃ bālasūryābhaṃ maṇiratnavibhūṣitam cikṣepādhiratheḥ kruddho bhaimasenir jighāṃsayā
english: Razor-edged, bright as the rising sun, adorned with gems and jewels—the son of Bhīma, in his wrath, hurled it at the son of Adhiratha, eager to slay him.

sanskrit: praviddham ativegena vikṣiptaṃ karṇasāyakaiḥ abhāgyasyeva saṃkalpas tan mogham apatad bhuvi
english: Cast with great speed but flung aside by Karṇa's shafts, it fell vainly to the ground like the resolve of an ill-fated man.

sanskrit: ghaṭotkacas tu saṃkruddho dṛṣṭvā cakraṃ nipātitam karṇaṃ prācchādayad bāṇaiḥ svarbhānur iva bhāskaram
english: But Ghaṭotkaca, enraged at seeing his discus brought down, covered Karṇa over with arrows as Svarbhānu covers the sun.

sanskrit: sūtaputras tv asaṃbhrānto rudropendrendravikramaḥ ghaṭotkacarathaṃ tūrṇaṃ chādayām āsa patribhiḥ
english: But the son of the sūta, unflinching, of prowess like Rudra, Upendra, and Indra, swiftly covered Ghaṭotkaca's chariot with his feathered shafts.

sanskrit: ghaṭotkacena kruddhena gadā hemāṅgadā tadā kṣiptā bhrāmya śaraiḥ sāpi karṇenābhyāhatāpatat
english: Then a mace ringed with gold, whirled and hurled by the enraged Ghaṭotkaca—that too, struck down by Karṇa's arrows, fell to earth.

sanskrit: tato 'ntarikṣam utpatya kālamegha ivonnadan pravavarṣa mahākāyo drumavarṣaṃ nabhastalāt
english: Then, leaping up into the sky, roaring like a cloud of doom, the huge-bodied one rained down a rain of trees from the vault of heaven.

sanskrit: tato māyāvinaṃ karṇo bhīmasenasutaṃ divi mārgaṇair abhivivyādha ghanaṃ sūrya ivāṃśubhiḥ
english: Then Karṇa pierced the illusion-wielding son of Bhīmasena in the sky with his shafts, as the sun pierces a cloud with its rays.

sanskrit: tasya sarvān hayān hatvā saṃchidya śatadhā ratham abhyavarṣac charaiḥ karṇaḥ parjanya iva vṛṣṭimān
english: Having slain all his horses and shattered his chariot into a hundred pieces, Karṇa rained down arrows upon him like Parjanya pouring rain.

sanskrit: na cāsyāsīd anirbhinnaṃ gātre dvyaṅgulam antaram so 'dṛśyata muhūrtena śvāvic chalalito yathā
english: There was not on his body a two-fingers' space left unpierced, and in a moment he seemed like a porcupine bristling with quills.

sanskrit: na hayān na rathaṃ tasya na dhvajaṃ na ghaṭotkacam dṛṣṭavantaḥ sma samare śaraughair abhisaṃvṛtam
english: Neither his horses, nor his chariot, nor his banner, nor Ghaṭotkaca himself could they see in the battle, so covered over was he by floods of arrows.

sanskrit: sa tu karṇasya tad divyam astram astreṇa śātayan māyāyuddhena māyāvī sūtaputram ayodhayat
english: But he, beating down Karṇa's celestial weapon with a weapon of his own, that master of illusion fought the son of the sūta with a battle of illusions.

sanskrit: so 'yodhayat tadā karṇaṃ māyayā lāghavena ca alakṣyamāṇo 'tha divi śarajāleṣu saṃpatan
english: He fought Karṇa then with illusion and with swiftness of hand, unseen, darting through the meshes of arrows in the sky.

sanskrit: bhaimasenir mahāmāyo māyayā kurusattama pracakāra mahāmāyāṃ mohayann iva bhārata
english: The son of Bhīma, that master of mighty illusion, O best of Kurus, wrought a great illusion, bewildering the foe, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: sa sma kṛtvā virūpāṇi vadanāny aśubhānanaḥ agrasat sūtaputrasya divyāny astrāṇi māyayā
english: That one of ill-omened face, fashioning hideous mouths, devoured by his illusion the celestial weapons of the sūta's son.

sanskrit: punaś cāpi mahākāyaḥ saṃchinnaḥ śatadhā raṇe gatasattvo nirutsāhaḥ patitaḥ khād vyadṛśyata hataṃ taṃ manyamānāḥ sma prāṇadan kurupuṃgavāḥ
english: And again the huge-bodied one, cut into a hundred pieces in the fight, seemed to fall lifeless and spent from the sky; and deeming him slain, the bulls of the Kurus raised a shout.

sanskrit: atha dehair navair anyair dikṣu sarvāsv adṛśyata punaś cāpi mahākāyaḥ śataśīrṣaḥ śatodaraḥ
english: But then, in all the quarters, he was seen again with fresh bodies, that huge-bodied one with a hundred heads and a hundred bellies.

sanskrit: vyadṛśyata mahābāhur maināka iva parvataḥ aṅguṣṭhamātro bhūtvā ca punar eva sa rākṣasaḥ sāgarormir ivoddhūtas tiryag ūrdhvam avartata
english: The mighty-armed one appeared like the mountain Maināka; and again that rākṣasa, becoming no larger than a thumb, rose up sideways and upward like a swelling wave of the sea.

sanskrit: vasudhāṃ dārayitvā ca punar apsu nyamajjata adṛśyata tadā tatra punar unmajjito 'nyataḥ
english: And cleaving the earth, he plunged again into the waters; and then he was seen there rising up once more from another place.

sanskrit: so 'vatīrya punas tasthau rathe hemapariṣkṛte kṣitiṃ dyāṃ ca diśaś caiva māyayāvṛtya daṃśitaḥ
english: Then descending, he stood again upon a gold-wrought chariot, mailed for battle, having veiled earth and sky and the quarters with his illusion.

sanskrit: gatvā karṇarathābhyāśaṃ vicalat kuṇḍalānanaḥ prāha vākyam asaṃbhrāntaḥ sūtaputraṃ viśāṃ pate
english: Drawing near to Karṇa's chariot, his face aquiver with its swinging earrings, unshaken he spoke this word to the son of the sūta, O lord of peoples:

sanskrit: tiṣṭhedānīṃ na me jīvan sūtaputra gamiṣyasi yuddhaśraddhām ahaṃ te 'dya vineṣyāmi raṇājire
english: "Stand now! You shall not depart alive from me, son of the sūta. This day on the field of battle I shall cure you of your appetite for war."

sanskrit: ity uktvā roṣatāmrākṣaṃ rakṣaḥ krūraparākramam utpapātāntarikṣaṃ ca jahāsa ca suvisvaram karṇam abhyāhanac caiva gajendram iva kesarī
english: So saying, that rākṣasa of cruel prowess, his eyes coppery with rage, sprang up into the air and laughed aloud, and smote Karṇa as a lion smites a lordly elephant.

sanskrit: rathākṣamātrair iṣubhir abhyavarṣad ghaṭotkacaḥ rathinām ṛṣabhaṃ karṇaṃ dhārābhir iva toyadaḥ śaravṛṣṭiṃ ca tāṃ karṇo dūraprāptām aśātayat
english: Ghaṭotkaca rained upon Karṇa, that bull among chariot-warriors, arrows the size of chariot-axles, as a cloud rains its torrents; but Karṇa beat down that rain of arrows while it was yet far off.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā ca vihatāṃ māyāṃ karṇena bharatarṣabha ghaṭotkacas tato māyāṃ sasarjāntarhitaḥ punaḥ
english: And seeing his illusion undone by Karṇa, O bull of the Bhāratas, Ghaṭotkaca, vanishing, sent forth yet another illusion.

sanskrit: so 'bhavad girir ity uccaḥ śikharais tarusaṃkaṭaiḥ śūlaprāsāsimusalajalaprasravaṇo mahān
english: He became a mountain, lofty, its peaks dense with trees, vast, streaming forth a flood of spears, lances, swords, and maces.

sanskrit: tam añjanacayaprakhyaṃ karṇo dṛṣṭvā mahīdharam prapātair āyudhāny ugrāṇy udvahantaṃ na cukṣubhe
english: Beholding that mountain dark as a heap of collyrium, pouring down dread weapons in its cataracts, Karṇa was not shaken.

sanskrit: smayann iva tataḥ karṇo divyam astram udīrayat tataḥ so 'streṇa śailendro vikṣipto vai vyanaśyata
english: Then Karṇa, as though smiling, sent forth a celestial weapon; and by that weapon the lord of mountains was scattered and vanished away.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa toyado bhūtvā nīlaḥ sendrāyudho divi aśmavṛṣṭibhir atyugraḥ sūtaputram avākirat
english: Then, becoming a dark cloud in the sky, hung with Indra's bow, most fierce, he poured a rain of stones upon the son of the sūta.

sanskrit: atha saṃdhāya vāyavyam astram astravidāṃ varaḥ vyadhamat kālameghaṃ taṃ karṇo vaikartano vṛṣā
english: Then, fitting the weapon of Vāyu, that best of weapon-knowers, Karṇa the son of Vikartana, the bull among men, scattered that cloud of doom.

sanskrit: sa mārgaṇagaṇaiḥ karṇo diśaḥ pracchādya sarvaśaḥ jaghānāstraṃ mahārāja ghaṭotkacasamīritam
english: Then Karṇa, covering all the quarters utterly with his hosts of arrows, destroyed, O great king, the weapon that Ghaṭotkaca had loosed.

sanskrit: tataḥ prahasya samare bhaimasenir mahābalaḥ prāduścakre mahāmāyāṃ karṇaṃ prati mahāratham
english: Then, laughing in the fight, the mighty son of Bhīma brought forth a great illusion against Karṇa, that great chariot-warrior.

sanskrit: sa dṛṣṭvā punar āyāntaṃ rathena rathināṃ varam ghaṭotkacam asaṃbhrāntaṃ rākṣasair bahubhir vṛtam
english: Seeing Ghaṭotkaca, that foremost of chariot-warriors, coming on again undismayed upon his car, surrounded by many rākṣasas—

sanskrit: siṃhaśārdūlasadṛśair mattadviradavikramaiḥ gajasthaiś ca rathasthaiś ca vājipṛṣṭhagatais tathā
english: rākṣasas like lions and tigers, with the prowess of rutting elephants, some on elephant-back, some on chariots, and some upon the backs of horses—

sanskrit: nānāśastradharair ghorair nānākavacabhūṣaṇaiḥ vṛtaṃ ghaṭotkacaṃ krūrair marudbhir iva vāsavam dṛṣṭvā karṇo maheṣvāso yodhayām āsa rākṣasam
english: surrounded by cruel and dreadful ones bearing manifold weapons and adorned with manifold armor—Ghaṭotkaca compassed about like Vāsava by the Maruts—beholding him, Karṇa the great archer gave battle to the rākṣasa.

sanskrit: ghaṭotkacas tataḥ karṇaṃ viddhvā pañcabhir āśugaiḥ nanāda bhairavaṃ nādaṃ bhīṣayan sarvapārthivān
english: Then Ghaṭotkaca, piercing Karṇa with five swift shafts, raised a fearful roar, striking terror into all the kings.

sanskrit: bhūyaś cāñjalikenātha samārgaṇagaṇaṃ mahat karṇahastasthitaṃ cāpaṃ cicchedāśu ghaṭotkacaḥ
english: And again, with an añjalika arrow, Ghaṭotkaca swiftly severed the great bow, together with its store of shafts, that was held in Karṇa's hand.

sanskrit: athānyad dhanur ādāya dṛḍhaṃ bhārasahaṃ mahat vyakarṣata balāt karṇa indrāyudham ivocchritam
english: Then taking up another bow, stout, able to bear the strain, and great, Karṇa drew it back by force, raised high like the bow of Indra.
